How To Read This

reflex-quant has the strongest relative profile in this run, 11.9% ahead of reflex by geometric mean. It takes 14 of 51 scenarios decisively, while reflex takes 5.

Each scenario was measured with all frameworks on one VM, on 3 independent VM sets, in 3 fresh processes per VM. The row score is the median of the per-machine estimates and its interval is their range; with 3 machines a range covers the cross-machine median with only ~75% probability, so it is not a 95% interval. The family-balanced leaderboard score is computed separately for each of the 3 machine sets (ratios within one VM) and the median is shown with the range; a ≈ next to a rank means the paired score ratios cross 1. Each workload group has equal weight in the overall score; the legacy flat score is also shown. With repeated estimates, ≈ and decisive wins use paired ratios on the same machine (or matched process rounds on one machine), rather than overlapping absolute time ranges. These descriptive ranges are not 95% confidence intervals. Single-process comparisons use median intervals. Censored rows record a cold-pilot budget exceedance, not a warmed median or its lower bound; they have no measured samples or exact score, and their frameworks are unranked. All intervals describe repeat measurements of this run, not the speed of a runtime on other hardware. Hover a row for its interval and noise.

Interpret wins through the scenario taxonomy: creation, update, pull/push propagation, dynamic dependency churn, large graphs, lifecycle pressure, and memory behavior can favor different runtimes.

Not ranked: @angular/signals (0 failed; 6 censored); @reatom/core (3 failed; 12 censored); @solidjs/signals (0 failed; 5 censored); @solidjs/signals 2 RC (0 failed; 5 censored); @vue/reactivity (0 failed; 2 censored); @vue/reactivity 3.6 RC (0 failed; 1 censored); alien-signals (0 failed; 1 censored); cellx (0 failed; 6 censored); dalien-signals (1 failed; 0 censored); kairo 0.8 alpha (3 failed; 11 censored); lite-signal (0 failed; 1 censored); MobX (0 failed; 2 censored); Preact Signals (0 failed; 2 censored); reactive-engine (0 failed; 13 censored); rescript-signals (0 failed; 2 censored); Signia (0 failed; 2 censored); SolidJS (0 failed; 5 censored); SolidJS 2 RC (0 failed; 5 censored); Svelte v5 (3 failed; 11 censored); TC39 Signals Polyfill (0 failed; 7 censored); uSignal (0 failed; 2 censored). Scoring incomplete measurements over only their completed scenarios would rank them on an easier workload set. Completed rows still appear in per-test cards.

Where The Noise Is

Spread of a row's medianTypical (median row)Rows
within one process±1.4%1387
between fresh processes±2.8%1387
between machines±12.8%1387
paired ratios between processes±4.2%1336
paired ratios between machines±5.5%1336

Each level is the standard deviation of ln(time), shown as an approximate relative spread, and includes the noise of the levels listed above it. The machine level compares per-machine estimates that are already medians over fresh processes, so it can be smaller than the process level. A within-process 95% interval only covers sample noise; in this run a fresh process or another machine typically moves a row 8.9x as much. Only the machine-level range reflects all three.

Paired spreads are SD of ln(time/reference time), using the same fully measured reference framework for each scenario. Processes pair by round within one VM; machines pair by machine round. Self-comparisons are excluded. These spreads are descriptive and help evaluate future sampling budgets.
